contents.name: Theorem 11.1: continuous H-valued traces for evolution-space functions
contents.reason: The local lemma proves the continuous H trace and gives the explicit trace estimate needed by the evolution-space argument.

contents.name: Lemma 11.2: evolution-space integration by parts
contents.reason: The local lemma proves the bilinear integration-by-parts identity and its squared-norm energy identity from the supplied mollification result.

contents.name: Theorem 11.3: variational well-posedness for the parabolic problem
contents.reason: The local existence theorem follows the controlling space-time BNB route. A complete local Galerkin argument proves measurability of the inverse action that the source leaves implicit, and initial data in H are reached by approximation from V.

contents.name: Section 12.1 method of lines: finite-dimensional mass and stiffness ODE
contents.reason: The local theorem proves existence, uniqueness, and energy stability for measurable coefficients in the finite-dimensional Galerkin system.

contents.name: Section 12.1 Rothe implicit Euler step
contents.reason: The algorithm records the implicit Euler step with exact interval averages so it is defined for measurable equivalence classes without point sampling.

contents.name: Section 12.1 Crank–Nicolson step
contents.reason: The local definition retains the autonomous midpoint form and uses the exact interval-average load required for L2 data.

contents.name: Section 12.2 conforming Galerkin methods and the cG(1)–Crank–Nicolson equivalence
contents.reason: The local algorithm derives the cG(1) equivalence by integrating its linear trial function and constant test function on each interval.

contents.name: Theorem 12.1: discontinuous Galerkin well-posedness
contents.reason: This theorem concerns a discontinuous space-time trial space, which the controlling plan does not include in this parabolic finite-element page.

contents.name: Section 12.2 discontinuous Galerkin time stepping and higher-degree implicit Runge–Kutta schemes
contents.reason: The batch is restricted to backward Euler and the cG(1)/Crank–Nicolson branch; it makes no claims about dG time stepping or higher stages.

contents.name: Theorem 12.2: dG discrete stability estimate
contents.reason: The estimate is for a dG scheme with symmetric autonomous form and additional discrete regularity, outside the controlling plan's selected methods.

contents.name: Theorem 12.3: a priori error estimate for dG degree zero
contents.reason: This dG(0) error analysis is a separate time-discontinuous formulation; the assigned methods use the stated continuous trial or backward Euler formulations.

contents.name: Theorem 12.4: a priori error estimate for dG degree one
contents.reason: This result concerns dG(1), which is not interchangeable with the cG(1) scheme covered by the local Crank–Nicolson item.

contents.name: Chapter 8, Theorem 8.1: Hilbert-space BNB inf-sup criterion
contents.reason: The source proves the inf-sup, continuity, and trivial-transposed-kernel criterion; the local lemma gives the full real Hilbert-space proof used by the space-time form.

contents.name: Chapter 11, §11.1: mollification in the evolution-space trace argument
contents.reason: The source uses time mollification in the trace argument; the local lemma proves translation continuity and smooth Bochner L2 approximation for arbitrary Hilbert targets.

contents.name: Chapter 11, §11.1: weak-derivative-preserving evolution-space mollification
contents.reason: The local proof supplies the extension, reflection, derivative identity, and L2 convergence needed by the trace argument without assuming separability of V.

contents.name: Theorem 11.3: weak compactness and limiting passage in variational existence
contents.reason: The source uses weak compactness in its existence argument; the local lemma proves Bochner L2 Hilbert completeness, separability, and closedness of the derivative graph.

contents.name: Theorem 11.3: measurable inverse-action detail
contents.reason: The source invokes the inverse action without proving its measurability; the local Galerkin approximants establish measurable direct and transposed inverse actions under scalar measurability.

contents.name: Section 1 variational formulation and Theorem 1.2 energy estimates
contents.reason: The local existence theorem follows the controlling space-time BNB route. A complete local Galerkin argument proves measurability of the inverse action that the source leaves implicit, and initial data in H are reached by approximation from V.

contents.name: Section 2.1 spatial semidiscretization and the finite-element mass-matrix system
contents.reason: The local theorem identifies the conforming finite-element subspace and applies the measurable-coefficient Galerkin ODE result.

contents.name: Section 2.2 Ritz projection and semidiscrete error-analysis setting
contents.reason: The local definition states the nonsymmetric bounded-coercive Ritz equation and proves that its solution map is well defined.

contents.name: Theorem 2.1: semidiscrete finite-element energy estimate
contents.reason: Its energy estimate is supplied as part of the local well-posedness proof after verifying the exact conforming subspace and form hypotheses.

contents.name: Lemma 2.2: semidiscrete Ritz error equation
contents.reason: The local theorem derives the full residual identity and explicitly retains the time derivative of the comparison error.

contents.name: Theorem 2.3: stability of the semidiscrete error
contents.reason: The local theorem tests the residual equation with the error and proves the energy estimate with its initial-error term.

contents.name: Section 2.4 consistency residual and noncommuting Ritz projection
contents.reason: The source's consistency issue is retained as the full residual for measurable forms, with orthogonality used only in the autonomous Ritz branch.

contents.name: Theorem 2.4: convergence of the discrete semidiscrete error
contents.reason: The local rate corollary supplies a conditional energy and L2 estimate and states the exact primal and adjoint approximation hypotheses.

contents.name: Theorem 2.5: convergence of the spatial discretization error
contents.reason: The local corollary keeps the dual regularity and approximation conditions explicit rather than assuming them for every polyhedral domain.

contents.name: Lemma 2.6: heat-kernel smoothing property
contents.reason: This smoothing result supports superconvergence and maximum-norm theory, neither of which is part of the assigned Ritz energy and L2 rate scope.

contents.name: Theorem 2.7: H1 superconvergence for linear elements
contents.reason: The theorem requires a specialized superconvergence setting and does not follow from the general shape-regular Ritz estimates assigned here.

contents.name: Theorem 2.8: two-dimensional maximum-norm estimate for linear elements
contents.reason: Maximum-norm estimates require stronger pointwise regularity and special estimates absent from the controlling plan's error-rate scope.

contents.name: Theorem 2.9: L2 superconvergence for higher-order elements
contents.reason: This result is a higher-order superconvergence claim, beyond the conditional primal and adjoint Ritz rate proved in this batch.

contents.name: Theorem 2.10: maximum-norm estimate for higher-order elements
contents.reason: The pointwise high-order estimate is outside the assigned energy and L2 error claims and would need separate regularity and approximation suppliers.

contents.name: Section 3.1 backward Euler and Crank–Nicolson low-order schemes
contents.reason: The two local algorithms preserve the schemes while averaging measurable forms and loads rather than evaluating representatives at time points.

contents.name: Section 3.1 Crank–Nicolson energy identity and discrete stability estimate
contents.reason: The local theorem proves the energy identity and separate maximum and cumulative bounds for the autonomous form.

contents.name: Remark 3.1 endpoint trapezoidal forcing quadrature
contents.reason: Endpoint samples are not defined for an L2 load equivalence class, so this quadrature option is excluded by the controlling no-point-sampling convention.

contents.name: Section 3.1 Crank–Nicolson consistency estimate and second-order rate under smoothness
contents.reason: The local theorem derives a complete H2 time-regularity error bound rather than importing the note's pointwise midpoint load assumption.

contents.name: Section 3.2 higher-degree continuous time discretizations
contents.reason: Only the cG(1) branch is assigned; no higher-degree time trial spaces or their quadrature rules are asserted.

contents.name: Theorem 3.3: general cG(q) energy estimate
contents.reason: The source theorem covers arbitrary polynomial degree, while this batch proves the backward Euler and cG(1) cases only.

contents.name: Section 3.4 consistency residual for the cG(1) restriction
contents.reason: The local proof derives the interval-integrated consistency residual for the cG(1) case and proves its H2 time-regularity bound.

contents.name: Theorem 3.4 general polynomial-degree time-discretization convergence rate
contents.reason: The source theorem covers arbitrary polynomial degree, while this batch proves backward Euler and cG(1) only; higher-degree time rates remain outside the assigned scope.

contents.name: Backward Euler first-order consistency and nodal convergence
contents.reason: The local result proves the first-order nodal error using the exact averaged-load residual and states its semidiscrete regularity assumptions.

contents.name: Section 1: time-dependent weak formulation and its L2(V*) load convention
contents.reason: The variational theorem absorbs the weak-formulation and load conventions while adding a full existence proof under scalar-measurable coefficients.

canonical.name: Separable Bochner weak compactness with Countable Choice
canonical.reason: The local proof establishes separable Bochner L2 Hilbert factors, a closed derivative graph, and the weak subsequence limit used by the BNB existence argument.

canonical.name: Fixed and operator-norm C1 comparison-projection product rules
canonical.reason: This local result supplies the derivative term and regularity condition needed for time-dependent projection comparisons.

canonical.name: Finite-dimensional Ritz equation existence, uniqueness and M/alpha bound
canonical.reason: The local lemma proves the nonsymmetric Ritz equation is uniquely solvable by a choice-free finite matrix argument.

canonical.name: Initial projection difference on the four-triangle fan mesh
canonical.reason: The companion-page calculation explicitly distinguishes L2 and Ritz initial data for the stated mesh and energy norm.

canonical.name: Direct finite-dimensional verification of the Ritz residual
canonical.reason: The companion example computes the finite-element mass and stiffness terms and checks the residual against the general identity.

canonical.name: Scalar H1 but non-H2 solution showing Crank–Nicolson order loss
canonical.reason: The companion example gives the exact first-step error and verifies why the second-order regularity hypothesis is needed.

canonical.reason: This local prerequisite proves completeness, separability, continuous dense inclusion, and the matching norm equivalence for the concrete zero-boundary finite-element energy space.
